paper_id: Semantic-Preserving Linguistic Steganography by Pivot Translation and Semantic-Aware Bins Coding
title: Semantic-Preserving Linguistic Steganography by Pivot Translation and Semantic-Aware Bins Coding
motivation: MLS methods have low payload; GLS methods have semantic inconsistency. Want high payload without sacrificing semantics.
problem_framing: Text steganography tradeoff between embedding capacity and semantic preservation across MLS vs GLS paradigms
key_insight: Use pivot translation (En→Ge→En) to alter expression while anchoring semantics in German pivot text
method_signature: En2Ge2En Seq2Seq model with Semantic-aware Bins coding for token-to-bits mapping
evaluation_criteria: BLEU/BERTScore for semantics, PPL for fluency, steganalysis accuracy for security
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Word-level causes many unknown tokens and security drops sharply (Fig.4)
evidence_for_taste: BPE and subword have become one of the core technologies
is also related to linguistic steganography
we leave the optimization for our future work
a sharp decline for the embedding payload
more likely to arouse the suspicion of the detector
thinking_moves: Bridge MLS and GLS by reframing paraphrase generation as a steganographic encoding opportunity
Anchor semantic invariance in an intermediate language (German) to decouple expression from meaning
Trade vocabulary coverage for subword granularity to eliminate unknown tokens that betray embedding
Accept that common-token strategies hurt payload; instead design semantic-aware bin assignment to preserve quality without sacrifice
